_meta.description: GradedFacts FR Source Registry — French national statistical body, legislature, constitutional council, and leading news outlets with independence and quality assessments.
_meta.methodology: Same tier and independence criteria as the US registry. Tier: primary = original data or official records produced by the institution; secondary = journalism citing primary sources; tertiary = aggregation or opinion. Independence: not implied by official status — assessed on documented editorial or operational independence from political direction.

schema.is_independent: true when no documented editorial control by political actors with a direct stake in outcomes
schema.affiliation_note: required when is_independent is false; explains the documented dependency

sources.name: INSEE (Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques)
France 24
sources.affiliation_note: France 24 is owned and funded entirely by France Médias Monde, a public company under French state control. It operates under a public service mission agreement with the French government and receives 100% of its budget through state appropriations. France 24 was established partly to promote French perspectives and influence internationally. While its editorial charter provides some formal independence protections and its journalism is of higher quality than state propaganda outlets, structural independence from the French state cannot be assumed. Official French foreign policy coverage in particular should be cross-referenced with independent sources.

sources.name: Cour de cassation (French Court of Cassation)
CNRS — Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
sources.independence_note: The CNRS is France's national centre for scientific research, established in 1939 and the largest fundamental research organisation in Europe. It operates as a public establishment of a scientific and technological character (EPST) under joint supervision of the Ministry of Higher Education and Research and the Ministry of Economy, but research direction and publication decisions are governed by elected scientific committees following peer-review standards. No documented political interference with research outputs. Its research units are embedded in universities and grandes écoles across France and it is the primary institutional source for French academic research data, publications, and scientific infrastructure.

sources.name: Libération
sources.independence_note: Libération is a French national daily newspaper founded in 1973 by Jean-Paul Sartre and Serge July. It has a centre-left editorial orientation and operates under standard French press freedom protections. Since 2014 it has been majority owned by Patrick Drahi's Altice group, with an editorial independence charter in place. While the ownership change introduced commercial pressures, no documented political party direction over news content has been established. Widely cited as one of France's leading newspapers of record.
